input.caption:
Tiramisu cinnamon rolls, la combinación mas fabulosa. ¡Seguro estos roles serán tus nuevos favoritos! ☕️🤍 #cocinaconricardo 
—
Lo que necesitas:
● Ingredientes roles:
○ 240 ml de leche entera (tibia)
○ 2 1/2 cucharaditas de levadura instantánea
○ 2 huevos
○ 90 g de mantequilla salada (derretida)
○ 100 g de azúcar blanco
○ 500 g de harina
○ 1 cucharadita de pasta de vainilla
● Procedimiento roles:
○ En un bowl de batidora agrega leche, una pizca de azúcar y encima levadura. Permite que la levadura active. Agrega huevos, vainilla, mantequilla y azúcar, combina. Agrega harina y mezcla hasta que todo esté a penas incorporado. Deja reposar 5 minutos.
○ Con el gancho, amasa por 5-7 min. La masa debe quedar suave y un poco pegajosa.
○ Transfiere a un bowl engrasado, cubre con plástico y deja reposar mínimo 2 hrs en un lugar tibio.
● Ingredientes base:
○ 113 g de mantequilla (temp. ambiente)
○ 100 g de azúcar mascabado
○ 50 g de azúcar blanco (refinado)
○ 30 g de crema para batir
○ 1 cucharadita de extracto de vainilla
○ 1/4 cucharadita de sal
● Procedimiento base:
○ Mezcla todo y coloca en la base del recipiente de tu elección.
● Ingredientes relleno:
○ 100 g de mantequilla (temp. ambiente)
○ 100 g de azúcar mascabado
○ 1 cucharada de cocoa en polvo
○ 1/2 cucharada (si te gusta mucho el café, 1 cucharada) de café molido espresso
○ 1 cucharadita de canela
○ 1/4 cucharadita de sal
● Procedimiento relleno:
○ Precalienta el horno a 180 C.
○ Con ayuda de una batidora, mezcla todos los ingredientes muy bien.
○ Extiende la masa. Cubre con el relleno. Corta, enrolla y coloca en el recipiente.
○ Hornea por 22-30 minutos.
● Ingredientes glaseado:
○ 225 g de queso mascarpone
○ 60 g de crema para batir.
○ 2 cucharadas de azúcar blanco
○ 1 cucharadita de extracto de vainilla
○ Cocoa en polvo (para decorar)
● Procedimiento glaseado:
○ Combina todo. Coloca sobre roles, y decora con cocoa. ¡Disfruta!
.
.
.
·
#tiramisu #cinnamonrolls #reposteria #rolesdecanela
input.transcript: La combinación más fabulosa, tiramisu cinnamon rolls,  que pudiera ser más perfecto que tomar dos postres icónicos  y mezclarlos para obtener un resultado verdaderamente delicioso.  Por un lado tenemos la esperada suavidad del rod de canela  y por otro lado tenemos los contundentes sabores de un tiramisu tradicional.  En este caso, uno de los ingredientes más importantes es el café,  pues además del más carpone el café es el ingrediente que más marca la pauta de sabor,  así que es importante utilizar un café molido de alte calidad.  Saben que una de mis cosas favoritas de cocinar es mezclar culturas,  sabores, ideas y descubrir nuevos postres.  Está ha sido una de mis combinaciones favoritas hasta ahora  y estoy seguro que les va a encantar tanto como a mí.  Qué fabuloso.

input.caption:
Mi flan cremoso de pumpkin spice es uno de esos postres que simplemente definen toda una temporada. Y este podría ser el más bello y reconfortante de todos. Creado utilizando los productos de @califiafarms🌱🤍 #cocinaconricardo 
—
Lo que necesitas:
● Ingredientes caramelo:
○ 150 g de azúcar (blanco, granulado)
● Procedimiento caramelo:
○ En un sartén agrega el azúcar. Permite que todo el azúcar se derrita a fuego muy bajo. Una vez que tenga un bello color y todos los cristales de azúcar se hayan disuelto, retira del fuego.
○ Mezcla delicadamente con un miserable de silicona y vierte el caramelo en el molde de tu elección. Permite que endurezca y enfríe.
● Ingredientes flan (puedes duplicar la receta para obtener un flan con la altura que muestro en el video):
○ 6 huevos
○ 150 ml de unsweetened almondmilk @califiafarms 
○ 100 ml de french vanilla creamer @califiafarms
○ 250 ml de leche condensada
○ 100 ml de crema para batir
○ 125 g de queso crema
○ 1 cucharada de pumpkin spice (2 cucharaditas de canela molida, 1 cucharadita de jengibre molido, 3/4 cucharadita de nuez moscada molida y 1/4 cucharadita de pimienta dulce molida)
○ 1 cucharadita de pasta de vainilla
● Procedimiento flan:
○ Agrega todos los ingredientes en una licuadora. Licúa hasta obtener una mezcla integrada y tersa.
○ Coloca un colador sobre el molde con el caramelo, y vacía la mezcla hacia el molde, pasando por el colador. Tapa.
○ A mi me gusta hacer el flan en vaporera o double boiler (como en el video), pero lo puedes llevar al horno poniendo el molde en una bandeja alta con agua hirviendo. En ambas opciones el tiempo de cocción es de aproximadamente 40-50 minutos (1 hora 50 minutos si duplicas la receta) hasta que cuaje.
○ Una vez pasado el tiempo, retira de la vaporera/horno y permite que enfríe a la intemperie hasta enfriar. Por último, lleva al refrigerador y que repose toda la noche.
○ Al día siguiente, pasa un cuchillo por las orillas y desmolda. Decora y ¡disfruta!
input.transcript: ¿Alguna vez habías visto un flan como este?  Pues este es mi Pumpkin Spice Flan, suave, sedoso y con una mezcla de especias que hace que toda la casa huele increíble.  También es perfecto para sentir que vive en el mundo Gilmore Girls esta temporada.  Y para hacerlo aún mejor estoy usando Califia Almond Milk sin endulzar y un poco de su deliciosos French vanilla creamer  que además de ser a base de plantas nos ayudan a elevar cada receta gracias a que son ingredientes de calidad.  Porque hay postres que simplemente definen toda una temporada y este podría ser el más bello y recomfortante posible  para cuando las hojas empiezan a cambiar de color.  ¿Qué fabuloso?

input.caption: 🤤 New Thai restaurant with TWELVE kinds of Pad Thai 🍜📍Bobo Thai @bobothaiusa #la #restaurant #recommendation #thaifood #noodles
input.transcript: This new Thai restaurant has 12 kinds of pad Thai.  It's actually the first restaurant in LA dedicated to pad Thai.  And as an Asian who eats more noodles than rice, I had to try it out.  First one I got was their classic, the 1938.  After the year Thailand named it their national dish.  I'm picking with pad Thai because it can sometimes taste super ketchupy.  But I didn't get that at all from this.  You'll be happy to know these are not tomato bites.  And in no key mushrooms on the topping, they're so satisfying to eat.  The second one I got is their two kings.  The flavor is just like a Tom Yum soup.  Very bright and citrusy and comes with tofu.  You can add toppings to any of them.  I got shrimp because tofu alone wasn't going to cut it.  Let's be real.  I can't lose further side dishes.  The pork jowl comes with sauce and a lettuce to wrap it in.  And I got broccoli to be healthy, I guess.  My next noodle was their happy place and is a pad cu.  I had a soft shell crab as the topping.  I always get pad cu at Thai restaurants and I'm still most partial to this one.  But the 2AM is a very close second.  It's a similar noodle dish but a lot spicier.  They have rice bowls too that they can't under the pad Thai umbrella.  I love how the Thai cook eggs.  They're the best.  And they came with Thai basil chicken.  Try the map they're called Bobo Thai.

input.caption: fall drinks are here! I tried every single drink at @essntlcoffeesd and I’m so impressed #sandiego #coffee #falldrinks #sandiegocoffee
input.transcript: Essential coffee in San Diego just dropped their fall drinks. They're in the college area and they're known for their Vietnamese coffee matcha and cream top drinks.  They have three different cream tops for their fall series. They have a brown sugar miso, a pumpkin pie cream, and a fig cream.  And you can get each one with either coffee or matcha. So obviously we tried both. The brown sugar miso was probably my favorite.  It was sweet and salty like the perfect balance and I thought it went really well with both the matcha and the coffee.  But the other two were also amazing. The pumpkin pie cream had so much pumpkin spice flavor and was just like fall in a drink.  And then the fig cream was super smooth and very lightly sweet which I really appreciated.  I just love that the drinks feel super fall without just being the exact same fall drinks. You see at every single coffee shop.  So if you're ready for some early fall drinks even though it's literally 90 degrees outside, this is definitely the place to go.

input.transcript: This is the best barbecue in San Diego and it's not even close.  Aalbi barbecue house in girl is right next to the beach.  They have really cool decor and they're dog friendly.  They have a lot of beer options so of course I had to start out with a giant crispy mickle.  And I ordered peaches a puppy patty.  We got a huge spread but of course I had to start with the brisket.  Insanely tender and falls apart in your mouth you barely even have to chew.  And this giant beef rib is so meaty and tender it's about falling off the bone.  And I love the chicken here because it is so juicy.  It's easy to dry out chicken but they never do.  They do sides insanely well here.  I always get the mashed potatoes with gravy.  Super creamy potatoes and a thick gravy.  I always crave this.  Now I am picky with my onion rings.  I usually prefer a beer batter but these are really nicely crunchy in season.  And for dessert you have to get the peach cobbler.  The crust is super buttery and crumbling, really juicy peaches and it kind of caramelizes the crust a little bit.  Actually some of the best dessert I've ever had.  Ooby barbecue house in girl always has a lot of good deals.  And it's family owned so go check it out if you're ever craving barbecue in San Diego.

input.transcript: We're trying all the best bakeries in Pasadena in one day.  First up, artisanal goods by car.  They're known for having the best chocolate croissants in LA.  This was the best chocolate croissant I've ever had.  Perfectly buttery and flaky, and the chocolate wasn't overly sweet.  Next, badass bakery.  They're known for their matcha cinnamon roll and cookies,  but everything looks so good.  We wanted one of everything.  We showed some restraint and only got the matcha cinnamon roll.  The s'mores brownie and a chocolate chip cookie.  The matcha cinnamon roll was super unique.  I never would have thought matcha and cinnamon worked together,  but it was so good.  The cookie was perfect.  Crispy on the edges and softened chewy in the middle.  The s'mores brownie was also so good.  Next, meal pain. input.caption:
This excellent $9.99 Nagahama style ramen spot opens to the public tomorrow Thursday 8/13 and is about to be best deal in NYC. 🍜 

I loved the lightness of the savory tonkotsu broth and the thin cut of the pork, and the spicy version packed a satisfying kick 🌶️🔥. I stayed quite close to this port area on the water during my trip to Fukuoka last year! The lighter broth makes this bowl of noodles perfect for all types of weather.

input.caption:
EASY MEALS FOR 2, EP. 15
Creamy Lemon Garlic Scallop Pasta
Ingredients
* 345g Hokkaido scallops
* Salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
* Oil, for searing
* 1 small shallot (about 42g), finely diced
* 4 cloves garlic (about 13g), minced
* ¼ cup water (optional for deglazing)
* ¼ cup water mixed with 1 tsp Hondashi
* ¾ cup heavy cream
* 150g pasta of choice
* ¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (plus more to taste)
* Juice of ½ lemon
* Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions
1. Cook the pasta
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until 1 minute before al dente. Reserve pasta water
2. Prepare the scallops
Pat the scallops completely dry with paper towels. Season both sides lightly with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
3. Sear the scallops
Heat a large pan over medium high heat, for the best sear, use a cast iron or stainless steel skillet, I didn't have one so I'm using a nonstick pan, the scallops still came out tasty ! Add a drizzle of oil.
Once the pan is hot, place the scallops in the skillet without overcrowding.
Sear for approximately 2 minutes per side, depending on their size, until a deep golden crust forms. Be careful not to overcook them or they’ll become rubbery.
Transfer the scallops to a plate and set aside.
4. Make the sauce
Reduce the heat to medium.
If needed, deglaze the pan with a splash of water, scraping up any browned bits.
Add:
* diced shallot
* minced garlic
Cook until softened and fragrant, about 1–2 minutes.
Pour in:
* ¾ cup heavy cream
* ¼ cup water mixed with 1 teaspoon Hondashi
Bring to a gentle simmer.
5. Finish the sauce
Stir in the grated Parmesan until melted and smooth.
Add the juice of ½ a lemon.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional Parmesan, salt ( go easy on salt if you're adding in salty pasta water later ), pepper, or lemon juice as needed.
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce along with a splash of reserved pasta water.
Toss until the pasta is evenly coated in the creamy sauce. 
#pasta #scallop #cooking #seafoodpasta #dinnerideas

recipe:

6) cook 2 scallion pancakes, add cheese on top of one
7) put chicken on top of the pancake and cheese & press the other pancake on & let it get crispy / melty

input.caption:
CHEESECAKE TIRAMISÚ 🔥🥳😋🫶🏼 la torta que no sabías que necesitabas probar, ahora tenés que hacerla para el finde! 😎😂. Es una deliciaaaa!
.
.
👉 Ingredientes:
Base:
Galletitas de vainilla o chocolate 300g
Manteca 150g
Relleno:
Queso crema 900g
Azúcar 200g
4 Huevos
Vainillas 1 paquete
Café fuerte (puede ser con licor también 😎)
Crema de leche 400cc (opcional, es para ponerle por encima de la torta)
cacao amargo c/n 
extracto de vainilla 1 cdta 
almidón de maíz 2 cdas

Paso a paso:
Procesar las galletitas y unir con la manteca derretida. Cubrir la base de un molde desmontable de 24cm.
Relleno: mezclar el queso crema con los huevos, el azúcar, extracto de vainilla y el almidón de maíz.
Colocar una capa sobre la torta.
Por encima colocar las vainillas previamente embebidas en café. Terminar de cubrir con la crema de queso y llevar al horno 170grados a baño maría por 1 hora.
Dejar enfriar y por arriba pueden batir crema a punto chantilly y ponerle encima o simplemente espolvorear xon cacao.  #cheesecake #tiramisú #recetas #pastry #foodie

• 7g instant yeast
• 12g sugar or honey
• 20g salt
• 45g olive oil (plus more for the pan if making a savory focaccia)

1. Mix water, yeast, sugar/honey, salt and olive oil. Add flour and mix until no dry spots remain. The dough will be STICKY!
2. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
3. Wet your hands and do 4 sets of stretch and folds, resting 30-45 minutes between each set.
4. Bulk rise 2-4 hours, until doubled, jiggly and bubbly.
5. Generously rub a 9x13 baking dish with butter (for the cinnamon roll focaccia). Pour in the dough and gently stretch toward the edges.
6. Preheat oven to 375. Add the cinnamon topping and dimple the dough.
7. Bake 25-30 minutes, until golden.
8. Drizzle the vanilla icing over the warm focaccia and let rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

CINNAMON TOPPING
• 1 stick butter, browned
• 1 cup brown sugar
• 2 tbsp ground cinnamon
• 1 tsp vanilla

VANILLA ICING
• 1 cup powdered sugar
• enough heavy cream to thin it out
• 2 tsp vanilla extract

A FEW TIPS:
• The first fold will be GLOOPY. That’s normal, do your best.
• Wet your hands every time you do stretch and folds or coil folds to prevent sticking. 
• Don’t stretch until the dough breaks. Be gentle and stretch just until you feel tension.
• Once the dough gets bubbly, be gentle when transferring. Those bubbles are what we want!
• Don’t obsess over the clock when doing your final rest. Look for dough that has doubled, is jiggly and fullllllll of bubbles.
• This recipe is a plain focaccia recipe, feel free to add whatever toppings you like!

Fas iniciar con una libra a roto de sushi que conseguís en cualquier supermercado.  Vas a lavarlo al menos 10 veces hasta que el agua salga clarita.  Lo preparás como dice las instrucciones del paquete y cuando esté listo lo llevas a una refractaria.  En una olla, gregas vinagre a roto. Terminamos con el arroz, damos vuelta con un plato, bañamos en una salsa sebichada,  se inilla damos un olí y listo.  Telen que hacerla.

input.caption:
📍République | Los Angeles

My husband told me about this spot that’s practically in our backyard, and somehow I had NO idea it existed. 

République has been around since 2013, but the building itself dates back to 1928 and was built by Charlie Chaplin! It later became home to La Brea Bakery and Campanile before becoming République.

input.transcript: These are all the best things I ate this month  as someone who works full-time in food media.  It's been so damn hot in LA recently.  So I ventured over to Malibu and went in Malibu,  you got a lilies.  Breakfast burritos are heavy on the refried beans.  I get it with Jody so, and it's perfect.  I'm also really into having soup when it's hot out.  So I figured it was a good time to try  Sawa Kaosoi in Studio City.  They give you all the fixin. And it's all thanks to Nailetta,  a pop of cart making them hot and fresh.  They've got interesting glazes like chili cinnamon.  I like them playing.  I like to taste the egginess.  I also love this lamb shank from Roshona Bilal.  You've been golly stripped, Malibu.  Actually, I liked everything I had here.  This chicken rice, the paratha,  and the family members that run the spot are so chill,  so nice.  I love it here.  I also made this video for work  on three rotisserie chicken spots,  all in Pasadena.  The first spot was rotisserie chicken of California.  They do this tangy, vinegary, 32 spice blend.  The second spot was Sausage chicken.  They're doing interesting Indian Mexican fusion,  like this Injaro rotisserie chicken.  Also great sides, Antertya.  And the third spot was Loli Farms.  I possibly the juiciest chicken I've ever had.  It's true, I'm not doing that influencer thing.  Well, I'm like, oh my god, it's the best.  Whole bird or sandwish.  Doesn't matter, it's great in juicie in every form.  And that's everything I have this month.  I will see you next month.

input.caption:
Noriko in River West Chicago is an intimate handroll bar where every roll is made right in front of you.

😋 What I ordered:
* Puncha Matcha
* Lychee Martini
* Nori Chips & Dip
* Modern Handroll Set
* Spicy Octopus
* Yellowtail
* Bluefin Tuna Toro
* Bluefin Tuna Akami

💵: $270

💭 Thoughts: The basement space has only 21 chef’s counter seats, dim moody lighting, and good music that isn’t too loud. You can watch the chefs make each handroll, making it a nice intimate dinner spot. 8.5/10.

Service was good overall. Everyone remembered our celebration and they surprised us with a card and complimentary prosecco, which was delicious. I also liked being seated at the end of the counter. My only issue was that we weren’t given ginger, wasabi, or soy sauce while other tables were, so I’m not sure if we were supposed to ask. 7/10.

The Nori Chips & Dip (8/10) had slightly oily nori, but the edamame hummus and chili crunch dip had a creamy texture with a nice little kick.

The Lychee Martini (7/10) was pretty standard. The Puncha Matcha (8/10) was more cucumber-forward than matcha, refreshing and very easy to drink.

The Toro (9/10) practically melted in my mouth, and the caviar added a nice pop of texture. The California (8/10) was surprisingly good with a nice balance of creamy avocado and crunchy cucumber. The Crab Motoyaki (8.5/10) was addicting with tender crab and a rich, savory topping.

The A5 Wagyu (6.5/10) was disappointing. I didn’t get much of the Wagyu flavor, and the crab cake and mayo sauce actually overpowered it. The Spicy Octopus (8/10) was one of my favorites with a nice chew and a good kick.

Everything tasted fresh, but most of the handrolls were pretty standard in flavor. Overall 7/10 for the handrolls.

📍 401 N Milwaukee Ave, Chicago, IL 60642

input.caption:
Gilt Bar in River North Chicago is a Michelin recognized American restaurant and bar known for its moody atmosphere and strong cocktail program.

😋 What I ordered: • Chocolate Martini • French Martini • Espresso Martini • Prosecco • Fried Chicken Sliders • Fried Onion Rings • Truffle Mafaldine • Steak & Ale Pot Pie • Prime Rib French Dip • Chocolate Layer Cake
💵: $210 + tip

💭 Thoughts: We joined the waitlist around 5:40 on Saturday and got seated within an hour. We ended up at a table near the entrance, so the atmosphere wasn’t quite as nice as the dining room. 7/10.

Service was top tier. 9.5/10. They genuinely cared about making things right when something went wrong. Our server even covered the forgotten Espresso Martini.

The Chocolate Martini (9.5/10) was creamy and chocolatey and dangerously easy to drink. The French Martini (9/10) was fruity and smooth. The Espresso Martini (7/10) was better than a lot I’ve tried but could’ve been foamier.

The Fried Chicken Sliders (8/10) were crispy, juicy, and perfectly coated in Nashville hot sauce without being drenched in sauce.

The Onion Rings (7/10) were crispy and oily with a nice spicy mayo.

The Truffle Mafaldine (8/10) was room temp, but the al dente pasta, creamy sauce, and truffle bits were heavenly.

The Steak & Ale Pot Pie (9/10) was fantastic. Tender brisket, flaky crispy puff pastry, and creamy mash underneath made it feel like short ribs and mash in pie form.

The Prime Rib French Dip (8.5/10) had tender, flavorful meat and au jus, but the bread was pretty plain.

The Chocolate Layer Cake (6/10) was a little dry and not quite chocolatey enough at first, but it got much better drenched in the hot fudge and paired with the vanilla gelato.

Overall, great time with amazing cocktails, top-tier service, and solid food.

input.transcript: This is how I think about beating pizza press using economics, because they charge a flat price for unlimited toppings.  Your monetary budget constraint completely disappears, meaning the marginal cost of every additional topping is identically zero.  So to find the optimum consumption bundle, you have to set the Lagrangian objective function where you maximize utility,  subject to a single non-monetary constraint, which I guess you could say is total crust capacity in this case.  You can correct me if I'm wrong here, because I'm a bit iffy on this one.  Under the Karushkin Tucker conditions, you don't simply add toppings until marginal utility hits zero.  You would add them until the marginal utility of each topping divided by its physical mass equals the shadow price of accapacity constraint.  Because I think if you cross that threshold, the marginal utility goes negative in the entire functional collapse.  But I think if you balance it right at the boundary condition, you can achieve a mathematically unconstrained global optimum.
